constraints: Returns a negative process number when called from a 4D Client, a positive one when called on the Server machine; single-user mode behaves like New process.
Returns 0 and generates a trappable error (via ON ERR CALL) if the process could not be created.
If param is passed, the name parameter must also be passed (cannot be omitted).
Pointer expressions cannot be passed as parameters to the process method.
Do not prefix name with '$' to make the process local in Client/Server mode -- unlike New process, this generates an error there (it works only in single-user mode).
If an object or collection is passed as param, a UTF-8 JSON copy is sent (not a reference); any pointers it contains are sent as dereferenced values.

overloadMerges.note: Added sentinelValues on 'stack' (0 = default/recommended stack size) and documented the optional trailing '*' marker's dedup-check semantics. Restored `returns` (Integer) from the parameter table's 'Function result' row -- apply_overload_merges replaces the whole overload from this merge entry's fields, so it was silently dropped even though the mechanical draft had correctly computed it.

params.description: Name of the new process; required if param is passed

If a process named 'name' is already running, reuse it (return its process number) instead of starting a new one

overloadMerges.semanticRole: Starts a new process running 'procedure' on the Server machine (Client/Server) or locally (single-user), optionally reusing an already-running process of the same name.
